article: History of Unicode and character encodings: ASCII, UTF-8, UTF-16, and emoji
findings: Made the difference between UTF-16 code units, Unicode code points, and user-perceived extended grapheme clusters explicit; linked Unicode UAX #29 and MDN String.length.
Replaced a vague statement about Japanese carrier emoji with the Unicode-defined 722-character set: 114 were already encoded in Unicode 5.2 or earlier and 608 were added in Unicode 6.0 in 2010.
Added primary/current references for Unicode Emoji UTS #51, Unicode text segmentation UAX #29, and IETF RFC 3629, while preserving the Unicode FAQ and Rob Pike history source.
Compared Japanese with all twelve translations, verified the numeric code-space/byte examples and Mermaid graph structures, and updated lastmod.

meaning.note: Compared the complete edition with Japanese: ASCII and its scope, legacy encoding differences and the Shift_JIS/Windows-1252 byte example, Unicode code-space versus assigned characters, UCS-2/UTF-16/UTF-8 distinctions, NUL and C-string caveat, UTF-8 ASCII compatibility/variable width/self-synchronization, surrogate pairs and JavaScript length, grapheme clusters/ZWJ sequences, and emoji standardization history.

terminology.note: Checked localized distinctions among character, code point, code unit, byte, encoding, Unicode scalar/code space, surrogate pair, grapheme cluster, UTF-8 synchronization, ZWJ, and emoji sequence.

mathematics.note: The article contains no mathematical derivation or calculation beyond code-space counts, which were checked as exact hexadecimal/decimal conversions and against Unicode documentation.

code.note: Compared both Mermaid diagrams for matching graph node/edge structure and verified the Shift_JIS example bytes and output text across editions. No code or diagram renderer was executed.

links.note: Verified six shared references: Unicode UTF FAQ, Rob Pike UTF-8 history, Unicode Emoji UTS #51, Unicode Text Segmentation UAX #29, IETF RFC 3629, and MDN String.length. Added the four standards/API references and contextual links in every translation. External reachability is not claimed beyond the documentation checks.
